negative_findings.description: Kosovo is not a MONEYVAL member and has no MONEYVAL mutual evaluation report. MONEYVAL covers Council of Europe member states (plus specified jurisdictions), and Kosovo is not a Council of Europe member. The seed query's premise ('MONEYVAL Kosovo mutual evaluation report') does not correspond to an existing document.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Kosovo MER exists. The functional substitute is the Council of Europe/EU PECK and PECK II project assessments (2018 round), which applied FATF/MONEYVAL methodology outside the formal evaluation procedure. FATF also lists no mutual evaluation for Kosovo.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analysts expecting a MONEYVAL cash-intensity assessment for Kosovo will find nothing and may wrongly conclude the data is missing entirely; the PECK II assessment and the EC country report AML chapter must be used instead, and regional MONEYVAL MERs used only as comparators.

negative_findings.description: No ECB or Eurosystem statistical series covers Kosovo's payment, card, ATM/POS or cash-circulation data, because Kosovo is unilaterally euroised without any monetary agreement with the EU (unlike San Marino, Monaco, Andorra, Vatican).
negative_findings.result_summary: ECB payments statistics, the SPACE study and euro banknote circulation series exclude Kosovo from their reporting population. ECB material on Kosovo is limited to policy/research framing of unilateral euroisation, not country data.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any figure on euro cash circulating in Kosovo cannot come from the ECB and must be a domestic (CBK) or estimated figure; treating an ECB series as the source would be an error. This makes CBK and EC-report figures the effective primary layer for A4 topics.

negative_findings.description: As of the searches conducted, Kosovo does not appear on the European Payments Council's list of countries within the SEPA schemes' geographical scope, while Albania, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Moldova and Serbia have been included.
negative_findings.result_summary: EPC list versions v7.0 (May 2025) and v8.0 (Dec 2025) were located; regional inclusion announcements exist for Montenegro/Albania (Nov 2024) and Serbia (May 2025), but no Kosovo inclusion announcement was found. Kosovo's status was not verified inside the v8.0 PDF text in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: SEPA scope membership is the pivotal structural variable for Kosovo's payment market; its absence means cross-border euro payments remain correspondent-bank priced, which materially shapes demand for domestic payment infrastructure.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language search for EU documentation on Kosovo's financial sector returns almost no Kosovo-specific material; general Cyrillic queries surface Serbian and North Macedonian national documents instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: The only reliable Serbian-language EU channel identified is the EEAS EU Office in Kosovo _sr document track (e.g. the SWD Kosovo report translations). No Serbian-language Eurostat, ECB or Council of Europe material specific to Kosovo payments was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Serbian-language coverage for this cell must be sourced from the EEAS delegation site rather than from generic search; otherwise the sr language requirement produces noise from Serbia proper.

negative_findings.description: Several key terms are ambiguous across the sq/sr/en searches for this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: 'Raporti i Komisionit Evropian' returns Albania's own EC report far more often than Kosovo's; 'платни промет' returns Serbian national payment-system material; 'Kosovo report' collides with EU Election Observation Mission reports; MONEYVAL queries return Serbia's APML pages. Queries must be pinned with 'Kosovë/Kosovo/Косово' plus a year and preferably a site filter.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without disambiguation the collector will ingest Albanian and Serbian national documents as if they were Kosovo sources, corrupting any A4 statistics baseline.

negative_findings.description: No EU-level machine-readable dataset of Kosovo card, ATM or POS statistics was identified in this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: Eurostat enlargement coverage for Kosovo is macro/social/ICT-oriented; the EC country report and ERP carry payment-infrastructure narrative rather than structured series. Concrete figures found in passing (KIPS volumes/values, cash transaction cap) trace back to the CBK, i.e. outside this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For A4 topics the EU/European layer supplies validation, framing and policy conditionality but not the primary numbers; the run must not expect this cell to yield the core statistical series.

brief: For Kosovo's payment and cash statistics, the EU/European layer is a validation, framing and conditionality layer rather than a data-production layer: the annual European Commission Kosovo Report (published in EN, SQ and SR via EEAS), the DG ECFIN Economic Reform Programme assessments, the SAA Sub-committee on Economic and Financial Issues and Statistics, and the Growth Plan/Reform Agenda milestones together give a compulsory, dated, comparable narrative record of payment-services alignment, SEPA/TIPS progress and statistical capacity. Eurostat covers Kosovo only through the enlargement-country products and through statistical-capacity assessments (the 2017 peer review and improvement actions), which matter chiefly for judging the reliability of Kosovo-origin numbers. Two structural absences define the cell: the ECB and Eurosystem publish no Kosovo payment, card, ATM/POS or cash-circulation series because euroisation is unilateral and unagreed, and Kosovo has no MONEYVAL mutual evaluation because it is not a Council of Europe member — the Council of Europe PECK II assessment applying FATF/MONEYVAL methodology is the substitute for cash-intensity and AML findings. The most decisive single fact to track is the European Payments Council's SEPA geographical-scope list, where regional peers have been admitted and Kosovo appears not yet to have been; EBRD Transition Report country assessments are the best European source of concrete retail-payment policy detail (National Retail Payments Strategy targets, cash-transaction caps).
